next_recommendation: PIVOT_COMPLETE - Dense embeddings characterized as COMPLEMENTARY views only. Three specific modes validated at 22-year/144k scale: (1) Citation Heritage View: center_projected_64dim AUC 0.7922 > 0.75 threshold, exceeds TF-IDF citation-based (0.71-0.74); (2) Cross-Lingual View: sachverhalt cross_lang_same_branch 0.2816 > 0.2, dispositiv 0.1502 > 0.1, erwaegungen 0.0941 > 0.05; (3) Linear Hybrid Complement: w=0.3-0.4 PASS both adversarial gates (JP 0.66-0.67) but BELOW TF-IDF baseline (0.78-0.79). True OOS JP ceiling ~0.53 confirms dense embeddings cannot be primary navigation. Minimal sufficient scale: 144k (22 years, 2000-2021) for citation heritage and hybrid complement; 174k with section extraction required for cross-lingual view. Data blockers: BGE/bger ID mapping + parquet 2022-2026 + section extraction at 174k (corpus lane resumption required). No further same-question cycles justified.

critical_findings.linear_hybrid: Optimal weight w=0.3-0.4 passes adversarial gates (JP 0.66-0.67) but remains BELOW TF-IDF baseline (0.78-0.79); improves cross-lang retrieval to 0.16 vs TF-IDF 0.124
critical_findings.v18_coarse_hierarchy: NEGATIVE - max branch purity 0.65 < 0.7 even at 4-label granularity
critical_findings.boilerplate_resistance: Dense embeddings MORE susceptible to procedural boilerplate than TF-IDF
